name: William Ward
bio: William Welsford Ward (1854-1932), Wilde's closest Oxford friend and the man he wrote to more often than anyone else in his twenties. He came to Magdalen from Radley as a Classical Demy in 1873, took a First in Mods and a Second in Greats, and went down at the end of 1876 to follow his father as a solicitor in Bristol, where he became a considerable public figure. His nickname 'Bouncer' came from a comic Oxford novel of 1873; Wilde's own was 'Hosky'. Wilde scratched a drawing inscribed 'Little Mr Bouncer' on the window of the room the two of them occupied in succession, and it survived until a college party smashed it in the 1960s. Ward wrote a short 'Oxford Reminiscence' of Wilde, published in 1954.
bio_note: Twenty-two letters. Dates: none recorded — his years are probably in the editors' note at the first letter; nothing is inferred here. The editors describe one letter, printed 38-9, as 'a letter of four double sheets' — by far the longest of the twenty-two. The register is bracketed by the ends of the correspondence: the earliest letter (printed 15, March 1876) signs off 'Your affectionate friend', the last (printed 112, mid-1881) 'Ever affectionately yours'. Two further correspondents surface in the record, neither on the map: John Addington Symonds, whose Studies of the Greek Poets Wilde was reviewing in August 1876 (printed 31) and who is a central figure in the period's homosexual writing; and Walter Pater, whose first letter to Wilde is printed whole at printed 59.
